concept.name: Net profit margin
concept.definition: Net income as a percentage of revenue - the final 'bottom-line' share of each sales dollar remaining after all costs, interest, and taxes have been deducted.
concept.intuition: It is the most complete single-margin summary: what ultimately falls to shareholders out of each dollar of sales.
concept.mechanics: Divide the income statement's bottom line - net income after cost of sales, operating expenses, interest, and income taxes - by net revenue for the same period, usually on a trailing-twelve-month basis for valuation work.
concept.formula: Net profit margin = Net income / Net revenue x 100.
concept.failure_modes: One-off items such as asset sales, tax credits, or write-downs can dominate a period's bottom line, so a single quarter's net margin is noisy; the margin also embeds leverage and tax structure, not just operating skill.
concept.misconceptions: A low net margin is not a sign of a bad business: a 2-3% margin grocer can earn excellent returns on capital through rapid turnover, while a 30% margin firm may sit on vast invested capital.
concept.example: Walmart's net margin runs about 2-3% while Microsoft's exceeds 35% - both highly profitable in absolute dollars, through opposite volume-versus-margin models.

citations.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Beginners' Guide to Financial Statements
